mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings and increasing the present value of equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or the average 20-day return in such periods is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6.0% over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, increasing the risk of recession and prompting equity investors to demand higher risk premiums, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in fewer than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.0% for 3 months, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in residential construction permits (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong underlying demand momentum, indicating robust consumer and housing activity that supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative or non-significant coefficient (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate, indicates weakening supply-side capacity and labor market stress, which increases the risk of stagflation and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in fewer than 60% of instances when both INDPRO is below its 12-month MA and UNRATE exceeds 6.0%, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above its 6-month rolling mean, coupled with a concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST), signals a strong rebound in private demand, boosting corporate earnings visibility and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of RSAFS above 6-month MA and HOUST > 1050.0 fails to generate positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term is not positive and significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 4.0% sustained for two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy regime, increasing the cost of capital and reducing equity valuation multiples, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in fewer than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0% for two months, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200k per month, combined with a declining unemployment rate, signals a tight labor market that may trigger wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, which increases equity risk premiums and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS > 200k and UNRATE < 6.0% fails to produce negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction effect is not negative and significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters, as measured by the latest available data, indicates a recessionary environment, reducing corporate earnings expectations and triggering risk-off behavior in equity markets, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate < 0% for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in fewer than 60% of instances when GDPC1 contracts for two quarters, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
